about: Which file does this URL name, and is it inside the root -- one set of cases for the two copies of the answer (FJS-D653): junction's transport/static.ts, read by test/served-path-vectors.test.ts, and sierra's serve/served-path.js, read through both of its origins by packages/sierra/test/served-path-vectors.test.js. Each copy found the symlink hole alone (FJS-746, FJS-783), so a case found by one is added here and the other is graded against it. Paths in files and links are relative to a scratch directory; root is the published one. Every link target is relative to that same directory.

verdicts.serves: 200, and the body is the named file's
verdicts.missing: 404 -- the answer a file that does not exist gets, so a way out of the root is not confirmed to whoever found it
verdicts.malformed: 400 -- not a URL, so not a file nobody has
verdicts.refused: any 4xx, in the server's own word: junction refuses a .. segment with 403, sierra normalizes it to a path inside the root and answers 404

cases.why: The control: a check that refused everything would satisfy every other case.
Containment is about where a link LANDS, so a link that stays inside is served.
An escaped ordinary character names the same file.
Two dots inside a name are not a segment; only a whole .. segment walks.
The control for missing: what every escape below must be indistinguishable from.
A link inside the root pointing out of it (FJS-746).
public2 shares public's string prefix; containment compares a path segment.
A directory link out of the root is refused until the operator names it.
Named in allowOutside, compared as a realpath, it is published.
A leading slash that survives decoding is still rooted at the root, never at the filesystem's.
decodeURIComponent throws; outside a try it killed the process (FJS-784).
A NUL truncates at the syscall, so an extension check reads .png and the file read is real.css.
The plain walk. A client normalizes it away, so it only arrives raw.
The walk escaped, which a URL parser also treats as ..
Two segments up from one level down.
An escaped slash is a slash once decoded, so this is one segment to a parser and three to the filesystem.
A backslash, which is a separator on Windows and a filename character elsewhere.
